# Proof of Crowd

> Evidence-based attention audits for crypto tokens. Measures whether a token's
> social conversation is carried by a real population or a small number of
> accounts, and whether that attention produced anyone who actually bought.
> Run by Nicki Sanders. Methodology is published in full.

The question an audit answers: a token's conversation spiked to two million
interactions. Did anybody show up? Manufactured attention and genuine discovery
leave different signatures, and the difference is measurable.

## What is measured

- **Creator concentration.** What share of a token's interactions come from its
  few loudest accounts.
- **Repeated wording.** What share of posts carry near-identical text across
  three or more separate accounts. One account repeating itself is a spammer;
  forty accounts posting the same line is a campaign.
- **Cross-token accounts.** What share of interactions come from accounts that
  also post about several other tokens in the same period.
- **Spam against the token's own baseline**, rather than against an absolute
  number, because some legitimate communities live in noisy neighbourhoods.
- **Decay signature.** Genuine adoption leaves a durably higher attention floor;
  campaigns leave a crater.
- **Supply concentration.** How much of the token is held by its largest
  addresses, separating wallets from liquidity pools, bridges, multisigs,
  exchange custody and burn addresses.
- **Attention-to-holder conversion.** First-time holders per million
  interactions on spike days against ordinary days, rebuilt from raw onchain
  Transfer logs.

## Engagements

- **Pulse Check — $500, 24 hours.** Single token, current state. Full evidence
  pack covering composition, baselines and the holder distribution, with a
  one-page written assessment.
- **Full Audit — $2,500, 5 business days.** Complete attention history with
  every spike classified, creator and campaign forensics, holder retention and
  attention-to-holder conversion rebuilt from raw onchain data, a 10+ page
  report and a walkthrough call. Suitable for listing applications and
  diligence files.
- **Monitoring — $750/month.** Daily detector watch, alerts on fresh spam waves
  or concentration shifts, monthly written report.

## Findings from the underlying research

Published across 35 open-source projects covering 6.5 years of daily data on
roughly 1,000 coins.

- About 85% of crypto social spikes are spam-heavy, and those carry no positive
  signal.
- The organic minority improves the odds of beating Bitcoin over three days from
  41.9% to 49.0%, which is the only comparison surviving multiple-testing
  correction.
- That edge is relative rather than directional: scored on whether price simply
  rose, it disappears.
- It requires the price not to have moved yet. The same spike after a 5% run is
  worth nothing.
- It does not work on stocks: 4,063 tickers, 9,073 events, no effect.
- Crypto attention has a roughly one-hour median half-life. What separates real
  from rented is not how fast it fades but who carried it while it lived.

## Integrity

- The fee buys the audit, not the answer. Conclusions follow the data, including
  for paying clients.
- Tokens held by the author are not audited.
- Reports describe measurable conversation patterns. They never claim to
  identify who is behind amplification, because identical wording is equally
  consistent with a paid campaign, an airdrop task, a quote-tweet chain, or a
  community handed a template.
- Social data comes from LunarCrush under a disclosed affiliate relationship.
  Analysis and conclusions are independent of it.

## Links

- [Home](https://proofofcrowd.com/): service, pricing, methodology
- [Sample report, organic verdict](https://proofofcrowd.com/sample-fet.html):
  $FET audited October 2026, scoring 23/100. Five attention spikes in three
  weeks with a growing crowd at each, an attention floor 2.4x higher than two
  months earlier, and an onchain conversion result that argues the other way
- [Sample report, manufactured verdict](https://proofofcrowd.com/sample.html):
  the $ZAMA spike of 31 July 2026, scoring 97/100. Both are published because a
  method that only ever finds problems is not measuring anything
- [Open research](https://github.com/nickisanders/lunarcrush-projects): 35
  projects, with null results published as carefully as the findings
- [Author on X](https://x.com/nickisanders)
